title: Vessels S2: DurisMUD movement and pacing
description:
Step S2 of the DurisMUD vessel study (`docs/ongoing-projects/vessels-ships.md`): movement and pacing (D1).

- **Momentum:** orders set a speed and heading; every 0.5 s vessel tick the hull converges on them at its class acceleration and turn rate, scaled by the sailmaster and the rudder, and covers speed / 90 rooms (speed 10 crosses a room every 4.5 s). Its position inside the room is kept; it crosses room edges in the order its track meets them (diagonally only through a corner), and each room entered is validated; a refused room stops the hull where its track met the edge.
- **Maximum speed:** design speed times the sailmaster, load, sail-condition, and terrain/weather/lane factors, SEADOG +1 at the helm, capped at 30; the class table sets the design speeds for new prototypes.
- **Moorings:** a hull at rest in port is berthed; `undock` casts off in 30 s, the new `anchor` holds a hull at sea and `undock` weighs it in 13 s. `setsail` is now the one-room maneuver (speed 6 or less, 5 s cooldown; `up`/`down` change altitude or depth).
- **Automated movers:** the autopilot steers (comes about in place when the waypoint is astern, slows for stop waypoints, casts off by itself); hunters steer and shadow their target; merchants cruise at design speed; `setschedule` and every scheduled departure validate the route by sailing a copy of the hull through the same steering and physics. New waypoints are reached on entering their own room. A hull that comes to rest saves its runtime row. Unowned hulls get their rigging made good when they berth.
- **Removed:** the old per-tick room step, manual grounding, and the draft barrier (the 3.3.2 crash check moves to S4, the refit rescaling to S3).
- **Also fixed:** `reglist type 5` and `pathlist`, broken since `500019db1`.
- Help is updated in `help.hlp` and the SQL components (VESSELS, AUTOPILOT, SEADOG, new ANCHOR keyword); `VESSEL_SYSTEM.md` has a Movement and Pacing section.

Review range: `vessels-s2-base..vessels-s2`. First review round: `vessels-s2..feat/vessels-s2` (one commit per finding, replies on each thread):

- `f58e6083c` edges crossed in time order (High).
- `e74d18928` the schedule check sails the momentum path.
- `bcc9435e0` room-scale waypoint arrival, with legacy migration 2026092901.
- `f6eb99cc8` owner loaded before the berth at boot.
- `808d1edc9` the Vailand Iron Passage re-routed clear of three coast clips that the corrected check found.
- `571ec69d0` a grace wait in the login helper for timed crew reports.

Verification (review round, 2026-09-29): `make test-all` passes with DB cases on (1890 CuTest cases). All 13 live gates pass on the installed review-fix binary, and the ferry soak passes again (2,735 s, 10 route completions, exact restart). All 33 jobs of the local CI matrix pass on `788f1ad67`.

Verification (S2 handoff): `make test-all` passes with DB cases on (1887 CuTest, including the new `test_vessel_movement.c`). All live gates pass on the head, including the new `test_vessel_movement_in_game.sh`: builder, tactical, lookout, boarding, narrative, rules, events, movement, frontier, derelict, campaign, merchant, and hunter. The ferry soak passes (2,736 s, 11 loops, exact restart) and a native 500-hull measurement averages 1.34 ms per fleet tick (`VESSEL_BENCHMARKS.md`, "S2 Momentum Re-baseline"). All 33 jobs of the local CI matrix (`scripts/ci/local/run.py`) pass on the head.

Deploy: no schema change. Boot migration 2026092901 moves `ship_waypoints` rows at the old five-room default (5.0) to 0.5. Re-apply `sql/components/vessels_campaign_content.sql` for the corrected Vailand waypoints; a merchant left on the old coordinates stalls on the coast, and its schedule is disabled at its next departure. Prototypes keep their stored speeds, so a speed-2 hull now crosses a room every 22.5 s; review slow prototypes with `vedit set <id> speed`.
